boundary_conditions.consequence_if_violated: Relationship patterns may differ in other geographic or cultural contexts
Findings may not apply to specialized populations or other regions
boundary_conditions.scope_text: Data is gathered by face to face survey method from 430 valid questionnaires

parsed_response.citation_summary: Turkish marketing study (abstract only) examining correlational relationships between Schwartz's value dimensions and hedonic consumption behaviors using survey data from 430 respondents in Kirikkale. No causal claims are made; only associations are reported. Study is not policy-relevant as it focuses on consumer behavior constructs without causal identification or policy variables.

empirical_parameters.display_name: Correlations between value dimensions and hedonic consumption
empirical_parameters.name: hedonic_consumption_correlates
empirical_parameters.transferability: Limited - single city sample, marketing context
empirical_parameters.value_qualitative: Benevolence, self-direction, tradition, power, spirituality, stimulation, and hedonism values are related to hedonic consumption dimensions (excitement and escape, innovativeness, pleasure and fun)

extraction_warnings: Only abstract available - no full text access
No quantitative effect sizes reported; only qualitative descriptions of 'related' variables
No causal claims made - study explicitly uses correlation analysis
No confidence intervals, standard errors, or p-values provided
Marketing/consumer behavior study with no policy-relevant variables
No experimental or quasi-experimental identification strategy
parsed_response.methodology: Cross-sectional survey study using face-to-face questionnaire administration. Factor analysis conducted for scale validation. Correlation analysis used to examine relationships between individual value dimensions (benevolence, universalism, self-direction, conformity, tradition, power, self-security, spirituality, stimulation, hedonism) and hedonic consumption dimensions (excitement and escape, innovativeness, pleasure and fun). No causal inference methods employed.
